hook.line: Sooner or later you will stand up in front of a room: a meeting, a class, a neighbours' assembly. A few set phrases tell the audience where you are in your talk and keep you sounding calm.
hook.es: Como pueden ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron en marzo.
hook.en: As you all can see on the screen, sales fell in March.

examples.es: Como pueden ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron en marzo.
examples.en: As you all can see on the screen, sales fell in March.

examples.es: Muchos de ustedes seguramente conocerán el café de Rosa.
examples.en: Many of you will probably know Rosa's café.

examples.es: A continuación, voy a presentarles los resultados.
examples.en: Next, I'm going to present the results to you all.

examples.es: A continuación, quisiera mostrarles una foto del café.
examples.en: Next, I'd like to show you all a photo of the café.
In short, we need more time.

examples.es: Para terminar, quisiera darles las gracias.
examples.en: To finish, I'd like to thank you all.

rule:
In a talk you speak to a group, so you use *ustedes* forms: *pueden ver*, not *puedes ver*.

Signposts:
*Como pueden ver…* = as you can see
*A continuación…* = next
*En definitiva…* = in short
*Para terminar…* = to finish

To guess what the room knows, use the future: *Muchos de ustedes seguramente conocerán…* (it means "probably", not "will in future").

When you present something to the room, *les* (to you all) sticks onto the end: *presentarles*, *mostrarles*. English has no such word.
smallPrint: Teachers call this formal public speech. The future in *conocerán* is the future of probability.

readAndPick.es: Como pueden ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.
options: As you all can see on the screen, sales fell.
As we can see on the screen, sales fell.
As I can see on the screen, sales fell.

readAndPick.es: A continuación, voy a presentarles los resultados.
options: Before that, I presented the results to you all.
Next, I'm going to present the results to you all.
Finally, I'm going to present the results to you all.
Next, we need more time.
However, we need more time.
In short, we need more time.

readAndPick.es: Muchos de ustedes seguramente conocerán el café de Rosa.
options: Many of you will probably know Rosa's café.
Many of you knew Rosa's café.
Many of you will visit Rosa's café.

readAndPick.es: Para terminar, quisiera darles las gracias.
options: To begin, I'd like to thank you all.
To finish, I'd like to thank you all.
To finish, I'd like to thank you.

readAndPick.es: Como podemos ver, las ventas subieron.
options: As you all can see, sales rose.
As I can see, sales rose.
As we can see, sales rose.

readAndPick.es: Quisiera mostrarles una foto del café.
options: I'd like to show you all a photo of the café.
I showed you all a photo of the café.
I'd like you all to show me a photo of the café.

readAndPick.es: Como puede ver, el barrio cambió.
options: As you all can see, the neighbourhood changed.
As you (formal, one person) can see, the neighbourhood changed.
As we can see, the neighbourhood changed.

readAndPick.es: A continuación, voy a explicarles el proceso.
options: Next, I'm going to explain the process to you all.
Next, I'm going to explain the process to him.
Before, I explained the process to you all.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *pueden* or *puedes*, then type the whole sentence to a room: *Como ___ ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.*
yourTurn.answer: Como pueden ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.
yourTurn.why: A room is *ustedes*, so the verb is *pueden*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Next, I'm going to present the results to you all.
yourTurn.answer: A continuación, voy a presentarles los resultados.
accept: A continuación, les voy a presentar los resultados.
yourTurn.why: *Les* means "to you all" and sticks onto *presentar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In short, we need more time.
yourTurn.why: *En definitiva* closes the point, like "in short".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Many of you will probably know Rosa's café.
yourTurn.answer: Muchos de ustedes seguramente conocerán el café de Rosa.
accept: Seguramente muchos de ustedes conocerán el café de Rosa.
yourTurn.why: *Seguramente* plus the future form guesses what the audience knows.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it for one person you address as *usted*: *Como pueden ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.* Say: As you (formal, one person) can see on the screen, sales fell.
yourTurn.answer: Como puede ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.
yourTurn.why: One person, formal: *usted puede*, so *puede ver*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: To finish, I'd like to thank you all.
yourTurn.answer: Para terminar, quisiera darles las gracias.
accept: Para terminar, les quisiera dar las gracias.
yourTurn.why: *Quisiera* is the polite "I'd like" and *les* sticks onto *darles*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Next, I'd like to show you all a photo of the café.
yourTurn.answer: A continuación, quisiera mostrarles una foto del café.
accept: A continuación, les quisiera mostrar una foto del café.

pitfalls.wrong: Como puedes ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.
pitfalls.right: Como pueden ver en la pantalla, las ventas bajaron.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Puedes* is for one friend; a group is *ustedes*, so *pueden*.

pitfalls.wrong: A continuación, voy a presentarlos los resultados.
pitfalls.right: A continuación, voy a presentarles los resultados.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Los* would be "them"; to say "to you all" you need *les*.
Almost. This is a fixed phrase and it ends in *-a*.

personal: Imagine you are opening a short talk. Say one sentence that begins with *Como pueden ver…* or *A continuación…*.
